requirements.description: RequestVote must reject candidates whose log is less up-to-date than the voter's log (compare last log term first, then last log index)
requirements.detail: Correctly implements Raft §5.4.1 log up-to-date check: first compares last_log_term (msg.last_log_term > my_last_term), then on tie compares last_log_index (msg.last_log_term == my_last_term and msg.last_log_index >= my_last_index). The >= for index is appropriate: a candidate tied on both term and index is exactly as up-to-date as the voter, and should not be rejected. log_up_to_date is then AND-ed with the existing voted_for check. Verdict confirmed independently.

requirements.description: AppendEntries must check prevLogIndex and prevLogTerm before appending entries (reject if the follower's log doesn't match at that position)
requirements.detail: Correctly implements Raft §5.3 prevLogIndex/prevLogTerm consistency check. Guards on prev_log_index > 0 (index 0 is the implicit log start, no term check needed). Rejects with two distinct conditions: (a) prev_log_index exceeds follower's log — out-of-range, returns last_index() as hint for leader to decrement next_index; (b) term_at(prev_log_index) != prev_log_term — term mismatch, also returns last_index(). These checks run before entry processing, preventing inconsistent appends. Verdict confirmed independently.

requirements.description: Leaders must only commit log entries from their current term (never commit entries from previous terms by counting replicas alone)
requirements.detail: Correctly implements Raft §5.4.2 current-term-only commit restriction. Loop iterates from commit_index+1 to last_index(); for each entry, uses `continue` to skip any entry where term_at(n) != self.current_term, preventing old-term entries from being committed by replica count alone. Quorum count (leader self-count + peers with match_index >= n) is only evaluated for current-term entries. Old-term entries are committed indirectly via the log matching property when a higher-index current-term entry achieves quorum. The sequential scan from commit_index+1 upward, combined with match_index tracking (which only advances on successful AppendEntries that include all prior entries), ensures commit_index progresses monotonically and entries are committed in order. Verdict confirmed independently.
